'''Jozef John Zwislocki''' (March 22, 1922 – May 14, 2018) was a Polish-born American neuroscientist. His scientific work focused on auditory neuroscience and the mechanisms of human hearing.
A native of [[Lwow]], Poland, Zwislocki attended the [[Federal Institute of Technology]] in Zurich, Switzerland, and taught at the [[University of Basel]] from 1945 to 1951. He left for a research fellowship at [[Harvard University]] and was a member of the [[Syracuse University]] faculty between 1957 and 1992.<ref name="jjzpapers">{{cite news |title=Jozef J. Zwislocki Papers |url=https://library.syr.edu/digital/guides_sua/html/sua_zwislocki_j.htm |accessdate=June 4, 2018 |publisher=Syracuse University}}</ref> Zwislocki held twelve patents.<ref name="jjzpapers"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Patents by Inventor Jozef J. Zwislocki |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/jozef-j-zwislocki |accessdate=June 4, 2018 |publisher=Justia}}</ref> Over the course of his career, Zwislocki was granted fellowship into the [[Acoustical Society of America]], as well as membership to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], [[Polish Academy of Sciences]], [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and [[Association for Research in Otolaryngology]], among others.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jozef John Zwislocki |url=http://www.isr.syr.edu/faculty/zwislocki.html |accessdate=June 4, 2018 |publisher=Institute for Sensory Research |archive-date=May 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528090618/http://www.isr.syr.edu/faculty/zwislocki.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He lived in [[Fayetteville, New York]], and died on May 14, 2018, aged 96.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jozef J. Zwislocki |url=http://obits.syracuse.com/obituaries/syracuse/obituary.aspx?pid=189008608 |accessdate=June 4, 2018 |work=Syracuse Post Standard |date=May 14, 2018}}</ref>
